---
title: "World Model"
description: "A learned model of environment dynamics used to predict possible future states."
term: "World Model"
letter: "W"
category: "AI Agents"
difficulty: "Advanced"
---

## Simple explanation

A world model is an internal model an agent uses to imagine what might happen
after an action, rather than learning only by acting in the real environment.

## Technical explanation

A world model approximates environment dynamics, often in a compressed latent
state space. It may predict next observations, rewards, or termination given a
state and action, and can be stochastic to represent uncertainty. The model
is imperfect; planning with it can amplify errors when imagined trajectories
move beyond the training distribution.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

World models can reduce costly or risky environment interaction and enable
planning or policy learning from simulated rollouts. Their value depends on
predictive accuracy over the decisions the agent will make, not just average
one-step prediction quality.

## How it works

Train a representation and dynamics model from trajectories. During planning
or policy optimization, initialize from the current observation, predict
possible future latent states under candidate actions, and select actions
using predicted outcomes. Validate plans against real transitions.

## Practical example

A robot can learn a predictive model of how its movements affect camera
observations and use that model to compare candidate motions before execution.
Limit rollout horizons or incorporate uncertainty when predictions become
unreliable.

## Common misconceptions

- A world model is not necessarily a complete, physically faithful simulation
  of reality.
- Better next-frame prediction does not guarantee better decisions; errors
  relevant to the policy matter most.
